page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-96 is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 96 dedicated virtual CPUs and 744.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core, positioning it for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM capacity per processing unit.

This instance type does not include local NVMe SSD storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators. All storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage options. Additionally, the instance does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning network configurations requiring external IPv4 connectivity must allocate these resources separately.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highmem-96 allocates dedicated physical CPU resources alongside a dense memory footprint, making it suitable for enterprise workloads where resource contention must be avoided. The lack of local storage and GPU accelerators reduces overhead costs for workloads that do not require local disk speed or parallel graphics processing. Appropriate workloads include large-scale databases, memory-intensive data processing, enterprise application hosting, and memory-bound simulation tasks.
